title: Stabilize orbit depth outputs and add npy viridis
objective: Investigate inconsistent/flickering depth output in examples/flashlight orbit render frames/videos, then update the render workflow to save raw depth .npy files and stable viridis depth PNGs. The current depth visualization sometimes becomes all black because per-frame visualization appears inconsistent; fix the visualization path so depth frames/videos are stable across an orbit.
instructions: Inspect examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py and any existing depth visualization patterns in examples/flashlight or nearby examples.

Investigate why rendered depth PNG/video flickers or becomes black. Focus on per-frame depth normalization, invalid/non-finite depth handling, channel shape/dtype assumptions, and OpenCV write/video expectations.
Add raw metric depth .npy output for every frame under each setting output, using a clear directory name such as frames/depth_meters_npy or frames/depth_meters.

Add viridis-colored depth PNG output for every frame under each setting output, using a clear directory name such as frames/depth_meters_viridis. Prefer a stable normalization across the whole rendered sequence for each light setting, or another defensible non-flickering normalization; document the chosen behavior in the result.
Update MP4 output so the depth visualization video uses the stable viridis PNGs, or add a separate viridis MP4 if preserving the old name is safer. Keep RGB output unchanged.
Update README/docs only where needed for user-facing output paths.
Add or update focused non-simulator tests for depth visualization behavior and output directory/video file naming if practical.
Run focused non-simulator validation. Do not require live SPEAR simulator.
expected_outputs: Root cause analysis for flicker/all-black depth output.
Files changed and new output paths.
definition_of_done: Render workflow writes raw depth .npy frames and stable viridis depth PNG frames for each light setting.
Depth video output uses stable depth visualization frames or a new clearly named viridis video.
